profile.acquisition: Acquired by Barclays Capital on 22 September 2008 as part of its purchase of Lehman Brothers North American investment banking and capital markets business. The bankruptcy court set the real estate consideration at 1.29 billion dollars, of which 330 million dollars was for the two New Jersey data centers, Cranford and Piscataway, together; the split between the two sites was not disclosed.
profile.capacity_note: No IT capacity, floor area or power figure for this site has been published by Lehman Brothers, Barclays, or the bankruptcy court record. Private corporate facilities of this kind publish no spec sheet.
profile.facility_type: private enterprise data center, financial services

reading.body:
Barclays Datacenter sits in Union County, New Jersey, as one of two New Jersey facilities Barclays acquired with Lehman Brothers' North American operations in 2008. The facility's IT power capacity is not published, so its size relative to AI infrastructure cannot be assessed from operator specifications alone.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities, but only 5 publish power figures totaling 111.3 megawatts. Barclays ranks sixth by published capacity in the state, meaning it either falls below the smallest published facility or publishes no capacity figure. Without a published figure, it cannot be placed in the state's infrastructure hierarchy.

The operator's own corporate site does not detail this facility. Its specific address, location, and current use remain outside the public record consulted by this site. Whether it remains operational, what load it carries, or which tenants it serves cannot be determined from published sources.
